---
title: "Env.SetFloatBits"
description: "Store an IEEE-754 bit pattern as int by key in the Env store."
---

Store an `int` (intended to be interpreted as an IEEE-754 bit pattern) for `key`. Useful when you want a scalar in `Env` and the value fits in 32 bits; values that need full precision or are out-of-range lose information at the boundary.

## Signature

```enforce
static proto native void SetFloatBits(string key, int bits);
```

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| key | `string` | The key to write. |
| bits | `int` | The IEEE-754 bit pattern to store. |

## Behavior

The store is locked; the kind is recorded as FloatBits. Reads via [Env.GetInt](./getint), [Env.GetBool](./getbool), or [Env.GetString](./getstring) on the same key return `0` or `""` because FloatBits is its own kind. The 32-bit `int` capping is the only lossiness: passing the bit pattern of a `float` is bit-exact; passing a value that needs more bits is not.

## Edge cases

- Writing past the 256-entry cap has no effect.
- The kind is fixed at write time. Pick FloatBits on the first write or the existing kind wins and your bit pattern never gets stored.

## Example

```enforce
Env.SetFloatBits("scale", 0x3FC00000); // bit pattern of 1.5f
```
